The words

Father, into thy hands alone
I have my all restored;
My all thy property I own,
The steward of the Lord.

Hereafter none can take away
My life, or goods, or fame;
Ready at thy demand to lay
Them down I always am.

Confiding in thy only love,
Through Jesus strengthening me,
I wait thy faithfulness to prove,
And give back all to thee.

Take when thou wilt into thy hands,
And as thou wilt require;
Resume by the Chaldean bands,
Or the devouring fire.

Determined all thy will to obey,
Thy blessings I restore;
Give, Lord, or take thy gifts away,
I praise thee evermore.

How to sing it from the solfa

  • Find doh first. Play or hum C and sing d r m f s up from it, so the whole choir has the key in their ears before you start.
  • Pitch the first note. The tune starts on s (G), on the first syllable of “Father”, as a pickup before the first full bar.
  • Count the time. 4/4 means four crotchet beats in each bar. In the grid every cell is half a crotchet: a dash (–) holds the note before it, and _ is a rest.
  • Know the notes. The tune uses d r m s l t and the chromatic fe. A comma after a note (s,) is the octave below; an apostrophe (d') is the octave above.

About the hymn

John Wesley printed these words in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 432. They first appeared in a book he and his brother Charles published together, and the Collection's own index cannot say which of the two wrote them.

The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.

  • Words: Charles Wesley (1707–1788)
  • Words: John Wesley (1703–1791)
  • Melody (1708): William Croft (1678–1727)

Tune ST ANNE by William Croft (1678–1727); words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788) or John Wesley (1703–1791).

Questions about Father, into Thy Hands Alone

What is the doh of Father, into Thy Hands Alone?

In this version, in C major, doh is C. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does Father, into Thy Hands Alone start on?

It starts on s (G in C major), a pickup on the first syllable of “Father” before the first full bar. Find doh first, then sing up or down to s.

Is Father, into Thy Hands Alone in the public domain?

Yes. Charles Wesley died in 1788, John Wesley died in 1791, William Croft died in 1727; the words were in print by 1780 and the music in 1708. Everyone named died before 1955 and both were published before 1929, so the hymn is out of copyright in the UK, the EU, the United States and Nigeria. Modern arrangements and translations can still be under copyright.
